messages.text: This is a test of background tasks. First, using the shell tool with background set to true, start "ping -n 4 127.0.0.1" as a background shell. Then, in the same turn and without waiting, run "ping -n 12 127.0.0.1" in the foreground (background false) and wait for it to finish. Then reply with one line saying whether you have been notified about the background shell yet. Do not poll the background shell.

content.text:
The user wants me to start a background ping, then run a foreground ping, then reply whether I've been notified about the background shell. These are dependent in the sense that they should be in the same turn but I need to call them sequentially? Actually they say "in the same turn and without waiting" - I should call both. The foreground one waits. I can issue both tool calls in one block? They're independent, but the instruction says start background then run foreground. Parallel calls in the same block would accomplish "without waiting". Let me do both in one block.

Background command `ping -n 4 127.0.0.1` takes ~3 seconds. Foreground `ping -n 12` takes ~11 seconds. So background likely finishes before foreground, and I'd be notified... The notification arrives automatically when it completes. Since I must not poll, and I need to reply after the foreground finishes, I should check whether I got notified in the meantime.

Let me issue both calls in one message.
